attempts.summary: Deployed PostgreSQL 13 streaming replication across node1 (initial primary), node2 and node3 (standbys) on RHEL 9. Opened firewalld port 5432 on all nodes, created a scram-sha-256 replicator role, and built standbys via pg_basebackup -R. Verified healthy async streaming replication and committed-data propagation. Simulated primary loss by stopping PostgreSQL on node1, promoted node2 to writable primary via pg_ctl promote with zero data loss (all pre-failover committed rows present, new writes accepted), repointed node3 to stream from node2, and rebuilt node1 as a standby of node2 via fresh pg_basebackup. Confirmed live writes on node2 replicate to both node1 and node3. Then ran the mandatory node-restart protocol: for each of node1, node3, and node2 (in that order, one at a time, preserving quorum), captured a pre-restart boot_id and health baseline, triggered systemctl reboot with an async wrapper so the ack returned before disconnection, polled until the node was reachable again, confirmed the boot_id changed, and verified PostgreSQL/replication/data fully recovered after each restart (node2 came back as the writable primary with all data intact and both standbys reconnected).
